output:
This change moves the workspace name limit (30 characters) into a shared constant, but one of the two live rename screens still lets people enter up to 60 characters. **Fix that before opening the PR.**

Mode: full review, in-session. For an 18-line diff I did the checks myself instead of spawning the per-area and paired checking agents. I confirmed each finding by reading the code, but two independent agents did not argue over them, so there is **no numeric score**. I made no edits and ran no tests.

**Scope:** 4 files, +18 −2 · base `00c0949` → `52841a5` (committed only, one commit: "fix(web): Add workspace name char limit").

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Fix first, then open the PR |
| **Blocking** | 1 finding (the settings rename page still allows 60 characters) |
| **Worth a ticket** | 1 |
| **Minor** | 2 |

### Fix before opening

**1. The main rename screen still allows 60 characters (P1, correctness)**
- **Where:** `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceSettings/sections/IdentitySection.tsx:12` (`const MAX_NAME_LENGTH = 60`), used at line 81.
- **What:** `IdentitySection` is what `/spaces/settings/general` renders, through `pages/spaces/settings/general.tsx` → `GeneralPage` → `IdentitySection`. It keeps its own limit of 60 and doesn't use `SPACE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`. The diff only caps `UpdateSpaceForm`, the rename dialog opened from the workspace card menus (`SpaceContextMenu`, `SpaceContextMenuNew`).
- **What goes wrong:** An admin opens Settings → General, types a 45-character name and saves. It's accepted, so the workspace now has a name longer than the new limit. If they later open the onboarding flow in edit mode, that name fails the `maxLength` check in `CreateSpaceOnboarding`, which blocks them there.
- **The comment is now wrong too:** the new doc comment at `apps/web/src/features/spaces/constants.ts:14` says the limit is "Enforced on both create and rename".
- **Fix:** delete the local `MAX_NAME_LENGTH` and use `SPACE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` at line 81. Add an `IdentitySection` test that checks the `maxlength` attribute; there is currently no test file for it.

### Worth a ticket

**2. The rename dialog shortens pasted names silently (P2, consistency)**
- **Where:** `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceSettings/UpdateSpaceForm.tsx:40`
- **What:** The limit is only the HTML `maxLength` attribute. Create (`CreateSpaceOnboarding/index.tsx:52-58`) uses a react-hook-form rule with an error message.
- **Effect:** Pasting a 40-character name into the rename dialog cuts it to 30 with no message. A name already stored at over 30 characters loads unchanged and can be re-saved.
- **Also missing:** this dialog skips the create form's special-character rule. That gap existed before this change.
- **Fix:** put the same `maxLength`, `pattern` and `validate` rules on the `Controller` (`rules={…}`) and show `fieldState.error`.

### Minor

| # | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceSettings/__tests__/UpdateSpaceForm.test.tsx:82-87` | The new test only checks the `maxlength` attribute. Nothing tests the create-flow limit or the settings page (see finding 1). A test that types 31 characters into `CreateSpaceOnboarding` and expects the error message would protect the limit in the flow that actually shows an error. |
| 4 | `apps/web/src/components/common/NameInput/index.tsx:24` (used by `features/spaces/components/SpaceCreationModal/index.tsx:76`) | This path allows 50 characters. Only its own test imports `SpaceCreationModal`, so it appears unused. Either delete it or give it the shared constant so a fourth limit doesn't come back. This is not caused by this change. |

### Checked, nothing found
- **Security:** it's a client-only length limit; no auth or input-handling paths change.
- **Performance:** nothing relevant.
- **Existing behaviour:** create is unchanged (30 → constant 30), and the message text is identical.
- **Structure and naming:** the constant sits in the feature's `constants.ts` next to `SPACES_LIMIT`. Importing `@/features/spaces/constants` from inside the feature matches the existing test at `SpaceSelectorDropdown.test.tsx:8`. Leaving the constant out of `index.ts` is fine because it is only used inside the feature.

### What this review didn't cover
- I didn't confirm the backend's real limit. `CreateSpaceDto` and `UpdateSpaceDto` in the generated store types have no `maxLength`, so the server may not enforce 30 at all.
- Tests, type-check and lint weren't run.
- Mobile wasn't checked; no workspace-rename code there came up in the search.
